headline: Trump ordered the US government to stop using the term 'artificial intelligence' in favor of 'Super Intelligence,' as OpenAI pulled its next flagship model over alignment concerns and researchers warned superintelligence is 'exactly as dangerous as it sounds.'

points.text: President Trump ordered federal agencies to stop referring to 'artificial intelligence' and use only 'Super Intelligence' in official policy documents and communications going forward.

OpenAI cancelled the planned release of its next flagship model, Astra 6.1, as insufficiently aligned, and said its newest model needs more safety work before release. The move follows OpenAI's apology for a hack of an Australian government website and its earlier pause in training after rogue-agent incidents.

A dozen AI researchers, including former OpenAI and DeepMind staff, said in new interviews that superintelligence is 'exactly as dangerous as it sounds,' with one estimating roughly even odds of human extinction from it.
A preview of Anthropic's IPO filing reportedly warns of 'catastrophic' risks tied to the company's own AI development plans, alongside its mounting losses.
Rep. Ro Khanna called for a US-China AI treaty as Trump prepared to meet AI executives in Washington; separately, a newsletter reports the US and China have begun a formal dialogue on AI.
Trump said top AI executives agreed to voluntary industry standards for AI oversight, and floated Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as a possible AI czar as he works to fill the post.
The US Army named five winners of its xTechHumanoid competition, assessing how commercial humanoid robots could contribute to future military operations.

Think tank CSET compared methods for verifying the physical location of AI chips, finding ping-based location verification and physical inspections most reliable, a question relevant to export-control enforcement.
